source.text: ה֥וֹי מֹרְאָ֖ה וְנִגְאָלָ֑ה הָעִ֖יר הַיּוֹנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe [to the] rebellious and defiled [one], the oppressing city!

en.L: Woe, rebellious and defiled one, \q the oppressing city!
en.B: Woe to the rebellious and defiled, \q the city of oppression!
en.R: How terrible it will be for the city that rebels and is unclean, \q the city that treats people cruelly!

fr.L: Malheur, rebelle et souillée, \q ville qui opprime !
fr.B: Malheur à la rebelle, à la souillée, \q à la ville de l’oppression !
fr.R: Quel malheur pour la ville qui se révolte et qui est impure, \q la ville qui traite les gens avec cruauté !

decisions.choice: the city: Jerusalem, not yet named
decisions.reason: The city is not named, but verse 2 speaks of "her God", verse 4 of her priests and the holy place, and verse 5 of the LORD in her midst, so it is Jerusalem. After the oracles against the nations, the woe falls on God's own city, as Amos 2:4-16 turns from the nations to Judah and Israel. |

decisions.choice: rebellious: defiant toward God
decisions.reason: The word is usually taken from the verb "rebel" (Deuteronomy 21:18; Jeremiah 5:23). A similar word means the crop of a bird (Leviticus 1:16), and some read "filthy", which would match "defiled".

decisions.choice: the oppressing city: the city that crushes the weak
decisions.reason: The verb means to oppress or treat violently (Jeremiah 22:3; Ezekiel 22:7, 29). The same letters spell the word for "dove", and some hear a play on it, but oppression is the sense here, as verse 3 goes on to show. |

decisions.choice: Woe (L), Woe to (B), How terrible it will be for (R)
decisions.reason: The cry follows the Isaiah table for hoy. Readable says "unclean" for "defiled" and "treats people cruelly" for "oppressing". |

decisions.choice: Feminine agreement for the city ("rebelle et souillée", "elle") through 3:1-20
decisions.reason: The Hebrew participles are feminine: Jerusalem, not yet named, is pictured as a woman, as the term sheet asks for personified cities.

source.text: לֹ֤א שָֽׁמְעָה֙ בְּק֔וֹל לֹ֥א לָקְחָ֖ה מוּסָ֑ר בַּֽיהוָה֙ לֹ֣א בָטָ֔חָה אֶל־אֱלֹהֶ֖יהָ לֹ֥א קָרֵֽבָה׃

records.literal_gloss: She has not listened to [the] voice; she has not accepted correction; in Yahweh she has not trusted; to her God she has not drawn near.

en.L: She has not listened to the voice; \q she has not accepted correction; \q in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} she has not trusted; \q to her God she has not drawn near.
en.B: She has not listened to the voice that called her; \q she has not accepted correction. \q She has not trusted in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q she has not drawn near to her God.
en.R: She does not listen when God calls her. \q She will not let anyone correct her. \q She does not trust {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q She does not come near to her God.

fr.L: Elle n’a pas écouté la voix ; \q elle n’a pas accepté la correction ; \q dans {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} elle n’a pas mis sa confiance ; \q de son Dieu elle ne s’est pas approchée.
fr.B: Elle n’a pas écouté la voix qui l’appelait ; \q elle n’a pas accepté la correction. \q Elle n’a pas mis sa confiance dans {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; \q elle ne s’est pas approchée de son Dieu.
fr.R: Elle n’écoute pas quand Dieu l’appelle. \q Elle ne laisse personne la corriger. \q Elle ne fait pas confiance {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. \q Elle ne s’approche pas de son Dieu.

decisions.choice: listen to the voice: obey
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice is to obey him. The voice is the LORD's, spoken through his prophets. Jeremiah 7:28 says almost the same of Judah: it "did not listen to the voice of the LORD its God and did not accept correction". |

decisions.choice: correction: discipline that teaches
decisions.reason: The word means instruction, warning and the discipline of hardship that is meant to teach (Proverbs 3:11; Jeremiah 2:30; 5:3). Verse 7 says that the LORD hoped his judgments on the nations would teach Jerusalem. |

decisions.choice: four "not"s: a complete refusal
decisions.reason: The verse is built of four short lines that all begin with "not". The city has refused every way back to God: it would not hear, would not learn, would not trust, would not come. |

decisions.choice: the voice that called her (B); when God calls her (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the voice" without naming whose. Balanced and Readable make plain that it is the LORD's call (m1). |

source.text: שָׂרֶ֣יהָ בְקִרְבָּ֔הּ אֲרָי֖וֹת שֹֽׁאֲגִ֑ים שֹׁפְטֶ֨יהָ֙ זְאֵ֣בֵי עֶ֔רֶב לֹ֥א גָרְמ֖וּ לַבֹּֽקֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: Her officials in her midst [are] roaring lions; her judges [are] wolves of [the] evening; they do not gnaw [anything] for the morning.

en.L: Her officials within her \q are roaring lions; \q her judges are wolves of the evening; \q they leave nothing for the morning.
en.B: Her officials in her midst \q are roaring lions; \q her judges are wolves at evening \q that leave nothing for the morning.
en.R: Her leaders are like roaring lions. \q Her judges are like wolves that hunt at night \q and leave nothing by morning.

fr.L: Ses chefs au milieu d’elle \q sont des lions rugissants ; \q ses juges sont des loups du soir ; \q ils ne laissent rien pour le matin.
fr.B: Ses chefs, au milieu d’elle, \q sont des lions rugissants ; \q ses juges sont des loups du soir \q qui ne laissent rien pour le matin.
fr.R: Ses dirigeants sont comme des lions qui rugissent. \q Ses juges sont comme des loups qui chassent la nuit \q et ne laissent rien au matin.

decisions.choice: lions and wolves: rulers who devour the people they should protect
decisions.reason: The officials and judges, who should guard the weak, prey on them. Ezekiel 22:25-27 uses almost the same pictures, and Micah 3:1-3 pictures the rulers as eating their people's flesh. |

decisions.choice: wolves of the evening: wolves that hunt as night falls
decisions.reason: Wolves hunt at dusk, hungry from the day (Habakkuk 1:8 uses the same phrase). With different vowels the word could be "desert" (Jeremiah 5:6 has "a wolf of the deserts"). The Greek translation is generally said to read "wolves of Arabia".

decisions.choice: they leave nothing for the morning: they devour everything at once
alternatives: they do not gnaw bones in the morning
decisions.reason: The verb is rare and is usually taken to mean "gnaw" or "leave bones" (compare Numbers 24:8). The wolves eat all their prey in the night, leaving nothing for the next day: the judges' greed is never satisfied.

decisions.choice: officials (L, B), leaders (R); like (R)
decisions.reason: The word is the one settled for court officials in the Twelve. Readable says "like" to make the comparison plain. |

source.text: נְבִיאֶ֨יהָ֙ פֹּֽחֲזִ֔ים אַנְשֵׁ֖י בֹּֽגְד֑וֹת כֹּהֲנֶ֨יהָ֙ חִלְּלוּ־קֹ֔דֶשׁ חָמְס֖וּ תּוֹרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Her prophets [are] reckless, men of treachery; her priests have profaned [the] holy; they have done violence [to] [the] instruction.

en.L: Her prophets are reckless, \q men of treachery; \q her priests profane what is holy; \q they do violence to the instruction.
en.B: Her prophets are arrogant, \q treacherous men; \q her priests profane what is holy \q and do violence to the instruction.
en.R: Her prophets are proud and careless. \q They cannot be trusted. \q Her priests treat holy things as if they were common. \q They twist God's teaching.

fr.L: Ses prophètes sont téméraires, \q des hommes de perfidie ; \q ses prêtres profanent ce qui est saint ; \q ils font violence à la loi.
fr.B: Ses prophètes sont arrogants, \q des hommes perfides ; \q ses prêtres profanent ce qui est saint \q et font violence à l’instruction.
fr.R: Ses prophètes sont orgueilleux et sans scrupules. \q On ne peut pas leur faire confiance. \q Ses prêtres traitent les choses saintes comme si elles étaient ordinaires. \q Ils déforment l’enseignement de Dieu.

decisions.choice: reckless: proud, careless, boastful
decisions.reason: The word describes people who are unrestrained and boastful (Judges 9:4). Jeremiah 23:32 uses a related word for the "recklessness" of prophets who speak lies in the LORD's name. |

decisions.choice: profane what is holy: treat holy things as common
decisions.reason: The priests' task was to teach the difference between the holy and the common (Leviticus 10:10). These priests blur it. The word may mean the holy things or the holy place. Ezekiel 22:26 uses almost the same words. |

decisions.choice: do violence to the instruction: twist the law they were to teach
decisions.reason: The word translated "instruction" (torah) is the teaching that priests gave from God's law (Malachi 2:6-7; Haggai 2:11). To do it violence is to misuse it for their own ends. |

decisions.choice: the instruction (L, B), God's teaching (R)
decisions.reason: The word follows the Isaiah table: "instruction" at Literal and Balanced, "teaching" at Readable. Readable adds "God's" to show whose teaching it is, and says what "profane" means. |

source.text: יְהוָ֤ה צַדִּיק֙ בְּקִרְבָּ֔הּ לֹ֥א יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה עַוְלָ֑ה בַּבֹּ֨קֶר בַּבֹּ֜קֶר מִשְׁפָּט֨וֹ יִתֵּ֤ן לָאוֹר֙ לֹ֣א נֶעְדָּ֔ר וְלֹֽא־יוֹדֵ֥עַ עַוָּ֖ל בֹּֽשֶׁת׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh [is] righteous in her midst; he does not do injustice; morning by morning his justice he gives to the light; it does not fail; but the unjust [one] does not know shame.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} within her is righteous; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does no injustice; \q morning by morning {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} justice to light, it does not fail; \q but the unjust one knows no shame.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} within her is righteous; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does no wrong. \q Morning after morning {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} justice to light and never fails; \q yet the unjust know no shame.
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is in the city, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} always does what is right. \q He never does anything wrong. \q Every morning, without fail, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} justice known. \q But evil people are not ashamed of what they do.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} au milieu d’elle est juste ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne commet pas d’injustice ; \q matin après matin {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} met {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} droit en lumière, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne manque pas ; \q mais l’injuste ne connaît pas la honte.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, au milieu d’elle, est juste ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne fait rien de mal. \q Chaque matin {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fait paraître {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} droit à la lumière, sans jamais faillir ; \q mais l’injuste ne connaît pas la honte.
fr.R: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est dans la ville, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fait toujours ce qui est juste. \q Il ne fait jamais rien de mal. \q Chaque matin, sans faute, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fait connaître {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} justice. \q Mais les méchants n’ont pas honte de ce qu’ils font.

decisions.choice: the LORD within her is righteous: the true judge in the city of corrupt judges
decisions.reason: The officials, judges, prophets and priests of verses 3-4 are in the city; so is the LORD, and he is everything they are not. "He does no injustice" recalls Deuteronomy 32:4: "a God of faithfulness and without injustice, righteous and upright is he". |

decisions.choice: morning by morning: every day, as surely as the dawn
decisions.reason: Kings and judges heard cases in the morning (2 Samuel 15:2; Jeremiah 21:12; Psalm 101:8). The LORD gives his judgment day after day, as faithfully as the sun rises. |

decisions.choice: to the light, it does not fail: his justice comes to light without fail
alternatives: at dawn he does not fail
decisions.reason: The words can be read "he brings his justice to light; it does not fail" or "at dawn he does not fail". Either way the LORD's justice never fails to appear.

decisions.choice: But the LORD is in the city (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds "But" to show the contrast with verses 3-4 (m1), and says "the city" for "her". |

source.text: הִכְרַ֣תִּי גוֹיִ֗ם נָשַׁ֨מּוּ֙ פִּנּוֹתָ֔ם הֶחֱרַ֥בְתִּי חֽוּצוֹתָ֖ם מִבְּלִ֣י עוֹבֵ֑ר נִצְדּ֧וּ עָרֵיהֶ֛ם מִבְּלִי־אִ֖ישׁ מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: I have cut off nations; their corner towers are desolate; I have laid waste their streets, with no one passing through; their cities have been destroyed, with no man, with no inhabitant.

en.L: I have cut off nations; their corner towers are desolate; \q I have laid waste their streets, with no one passing through; \q their cities are destroyed, without a person, without an inhabitant.
en.B: I have cut off nations; their towers lie in ruins. \q I have left their streets deserted, with no one walking through them. \q Their cities are laid waste; no one is left, no one lives there.
en.R: I have destroyed nations. Their strong towers are in ruins. \q I have made their streets empty, and no one walks through them. \q Their cities are destroyed, and no one lives there anymore.

fr.L: J’ai retranché des nations ; leurs tours d’angle sont désolées ; \q j’ai dévasté leurs rues, sans personne qui y passe ; \q leurs villes sont détruites, sans personne, sans habitant.
fr.B: J’ai retranché des nations ; leurs tours sont en ruines. \q J’ai vidé leurs rues ; plus personne n’y passe. \q Leurs villes sont ravagées ; il ne reste personne, plus un habitant.
fr.R: J’ai détruit des nations. Leurs tours fortifiées sont en ruines. \q J’ai vidé leurs rues, et personne n’y passe plus. \q Leurs villes sont détruites, et plus personne n’y habite.

decisions.choice: I have cut off nations: the LORD points to his judgments on other nations
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks again. The nations he has already judged were a warning that Jerusalem should have heeded (verse 7). They are not named. |

decisions.choice: corner towers: the towers at the corners of a city's walls
decisions.reason: The word means "corners", the strongest points of the walls, as in 1:16. |

decisions.choice: their towers (B), their strong towers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "towers" for the corners of the walls (m2), as at 1:16. |

source.text: אָמַ֜רְתִּי אַךְ־תִּירְאִ֤י אוֹתִי֙ תִּקְחִ֣י מוּסָ֔ר וְלֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֣ת מְעוֹנָ֔הּ כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־פָּקַ֖דְתִּי עָלֶ֑יהָ אָכֵן֙ הִשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ הִשְׁחִ֔יתוּ כֹּ֖ל עֲלִילוֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: I said, Surely you will fear me; you will accept correction; and her dwelling will not be cut off, all that I have appointed against her; but they rose early, they corrupted all their deeds.

en.L: I said, "Surely you will fear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q you will accept correction"; \q so her dwelling would not be cut off, \q [for] all that I had appointed against her. \q But they rose early; they corrupted all their deeds.
en.B: I said, "Surely now you will fear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} \q and accept correction." \q Then her dwelling would not be cut off \q for all the punishment I had decided for her. \q But they were all the more eager to make all their deeds corrupt.
en.R: I thought, "Surely now you will fear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} \q and learn from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} correction." \q Then the city would not be destroyed \q by all the punishments I had planned for it. \q But the people were eager to keep doing every kind of evil.

fr.L: J’ai dit : « Sûrement tu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} craindras ; \q tu accepteras la correction » ; \q ainsi sa demeure ne serait pas retranchée, \q [selon] tout ce que j’avais décidé contre elle. \q Mais ils se sont levés tôt ; ils ont corrompu toutes leurs actions.
fr.B: J’ai dit : « Maintenant, sûrement, tu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} craindras \q et tu accepteras la correction. » \q Alors sa demeure ne serait pas retranchée \q malgré toute la punition que j’avais décidée contre elle. \q Mais ils ont mis encore plus d’ardeur à corrompre toutes leurs actions.
fr.R: Je pensais : « Maintenant, sûrement, tu vas {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} craindre \q et tirer la leçon de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} correction. » \q Alors la ville ne serait pas détruite \q par toutes les punitions que j’avais prévues contre elle. \q Mais les gens se sont empressés de continuer à faire toutes sortes de mal.

decisions.choice: you ... her ... they: the city addressed, then spoken of, then its people
decisions.reason: The LORD tells what he hoped: he speaks to the city ("you"), then about it ("her"), then about its people ("they"). Such shifts are common in the prophets. His hope was that the judgments of verse 6 would teach Jerusalem to fear him. |

decisions.choice: her dwelling would not be cut off, for all that I had appointed against her
alternatives: it would not be cut off from her eyes
decisions.reason: The line is hard. "Her dwelling" is the city itself, and "all that I appointed against her" is the punishment the LORD had decided, which would not have come if she had learned. The verb can also mean "punish", giving "however much I punished her". The Greek translation is generally said to read "from her eyes" for "her dwelling", a difference of one letter.

decisions.choice: they rose early: they were eager
decisions.reason: To rise early to do something is to do it eagerly and at once. Jeremiah uses the same idiom of the LORD "rising early" to send his prophets (Jeremiah 7:13, 25). Here the people are eager only to do wrong. |

decisions.choice: they were all the more eager (B); were eager to keep doing (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m3). The LORD's own words are quoted in double quotes, as speech within the oracle. |

decisions.choice: "tu" with feminine agreement for the city addressed, "elle" when spoken of, "ils" for its people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew changes person within the verse (singular feminine "you", "her", plural "they"); French follows each change, as the term sheet asks.

source.text: לָכֵ֤ן חַכּוּ־לִי֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה לְי֖וֹם קוּמִ֣י לְעַ֑ד כִּ֣י מִשְׁפָּטִי֩ לֶאֱסֹ֨ף גּוֹיִ֜ם לְקָבְצִ֣י מַמְלָכ֗וֹת לִשְׁפֹּ֨ךְ עֲלֵיהֶ֤ם זַעְמִי֙ כֹּ֚ל חֲר֣וֹן אַפִּ֔י כִּ֚י בְּאֵ֣שׁ קִנְאָתִ֔י תֵּאָכֵ֖ל כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore wait for me, declaration of Yahweh, for [the] day of my rising up for plunder; for my decision [is] to gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, to pour out on them my indignation, all [the] burning of my anger; for in [the] fire of my jealousy all the earth will be consumed.

en.L: Therefore wait for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q for the day when I rise up for plunder; \q for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} decision is to gather nations, to bring kingdoms together, to pour out on them {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} indignation, all the burning of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger; \q for in the fire of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} jealousy \q all the earth will be consumed.
en.B: So wait for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q for the day when I rise up to seize the plunder. \q For I have decided to gather the nations and assemble the kingdoms, to pour out on them {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fury, all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} burning anger; \q for in the fire of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} jealous anger \q the whole earth will be consumed.
en.R: So wait for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Wait for the day when I rise up to take the spoils of war. \q I have decided to gather the nations and bring the kingdoms together. I will pour out on them all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fierce anger. \q My jealous anger will burn like fire \q and destroy the whole earth.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi attendez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q pour le jour où je me lèverai pour le butin ; \q car {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} décision est de rassembler des nations, de réunir des royaumes, pour répandre sur eux {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} indignation, toute l’ardeur de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère ; \q car dans le feu de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} jalousie \q toute la terre sera dévorée.
fr.B: Alors attendez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q attendez le jour où je me lèverai pour saisir le butin. \q Car j’ai décidé de rassembler les nations et de réunir les royaumes, pour répandre sur eux {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur, toute l’ardeur de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère ; \q car dans le feu de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère jalouse \q toute la terre sera dévorée.
fr.R: Alors attendez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. \q Attendez le jour où je me lèverai pour prendre le butin de guerre. \q J’ai décidé de rassembler les nations et de réunir les royaumes. Je déverserai sur eux toute {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} terrible colère. \q Ma colère jalouse brûlera comme un feu \q et détruira toute la terre.

decisions.choice: wait for me: addressed to those who are faithful, or a warning to the city
decisions.reason: The command is plural. After verse 7 it may warn the corrupt city to wait for its judgment. But "wait for" the LORD usually means to hope in him (Isaiah 8:17; 30:18; Habakkuk 2:3), and the verses that follow turn to promise, so it is more likely addressed to the humble of 2:3, who are to wait for the day when the LORD judges the nations and renews his people.

decisions.choice: for plunder: to seize the spoils as a warrior
decisions.reason: The Hebrew vowels read "for plunder". With other vowels the same letters mean "as a witness", and the Greek and Syriac translations are generally said to read it so: the LORD rises to testify against the nations.

decisions.choice: in the fire of my jealousy all the earth will be consumed: the words of 1:18
decisions.reason: The line repeats 1:18, now in the LORD's own voice. The gathering of the nations for judgment recalls Joel 4:2, 12. The earth consumed here is the world of the nations; the verses that follow speak of peoples who survive it and call on the LORD's name. |

decisions.choice: a verse with every letter of the alphabet
decisions.reason: Jewish scribal tradition notes that this is the only verse in the Hebrew Bible that contains every letter of the Hebrew alphabet, including the special final forms. |

decisions.choice: the wording of 1:18 at each level; for plunder (L), to seize the plunder (B), to take the spoils of war (R)
decisions.reason: Where the line repeats 1:18, each level uses its wording there, with "my" for "his": "in the fire of my jealousy all the earth will be consumed" (L), "in the fire of my jealous anger the whole earth will be consumed" (B), "My jealous anger will burn like fire and destroy the whole earth" (R). Readable splits the long middle line into two sentences. |

decisions.choice: The last line keeps the French wording of 1:18 at each level ("dans le feu de ma jalousie toute la terre sera dévorée" L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats 1:18 word for word, so French does too, as the English.

source.text: כִּֽי־אָ֛ז אֶהְפֹּ֥ךְ אֶל־עַמִּ֖ים שָׂפָ֣ה בְרוּרָ֑ה לִקְרֹ֤א כֻלָּם֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה לְעָבְד֖וֹ שְׁכֶ֥ם אֶחָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: For then I will change for [the] peoples a lip [into a] purified [one], that all of them may call on [the] name of Yahweh, to serve him [with] one shoulder.

en.L: For then I will change the peoples to a purified lip, \q that all of them may call on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with one shoulder.
en.B: Then I will purify the speech of the peoples, \q so that all of them may call on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} shoulder to shoulder.
en.R: Then I will change the nations and make their speech pure, \q so that all of them can worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} together.

fr.L: Car alors je changerai pour les peuples [leur] lèvre en une lèvre purifiée, \q afin que tous invoquent le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servir d’une seule épaule.
fr.B: Alors je purifierai le langage des peuples, \q pour que tous invoquent le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} \q et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servent d’un même cœur, coude à coude.
fr.R: Alors je changerai les nations et je rendrai leur langage pur, \q pour que toutes puissent adorer {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} \q et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servir ensemble.

decisions.choice: a purified lip: a reversal of Babel
decisions.reason: In Hebrew "lip" also means "speech" or "language". At Babel all the earth had "one lip", and the LORD confused it and scattered the peoples (Genesis 11:1-9). Here he purifies the peoples' lip so that all of them call on his name together. |

decisions.choice: a pure lip, to call on the name of the LORD: speech cleansed of the names of other gods
decisions.reason: Lips are made clean so that they can speak to God (Isaiah 6:5-7). Hosea 2:19 promises that the names of the Baals will be removed from Israel's mouth. To call on the LORD's name is to worship him and pray to him (Genesis 12:8; Joel 3:5). |

decisions.choice: with one shoulder: side by side, as one
decisions.reason: The picture is of people carrying one load together, or of oxen under one yoke. They serve the LORD in unity. |

decisions.choice: a purified lip (L), the speech (B, R); with one shoulder (L), shoulder to shoulder (B), together (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "lip", which recalls Babel (m1). Balanced and Readable give its sense, "speech". Readable says "worship the LORD" for "call on the name of the LORD" (m2). |

source.text: מֵעֵ֖בֶר לְנַֽהֲרֵי־כ֑וּשׁ עֲתָרַי֙ בַּת־פוּצַ֔ייוֹבִל֖וּן מִנְחָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: From beyond [the] rivers of Cush my worshipers, [the] daughter of my scattered ones, will bring my offering.

en.L: From beyond the rivers of Cush \q {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} worshipers, the daughter of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} scattered ones, \q will bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} offering.
en.B: From beyond the rivers of Cush \q those who pray to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} scattered people, \q will bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} offerings.
en.R: People who worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will come from beyond the rivers of Cush, south of Egypt. \q My people who were scattered \q will bring gifts to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

fr.L: D’au-delà des fleuves de Koush, \q {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} adorateurs, la fille de {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} dispersés, \q apporteront {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} offrande.
fr.B: D’au-delà des fleuves de Koush, \q ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} prient, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple dispersé, \q {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}apporteront des offrandes.
fr.R: Des gens qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}adorent viendront d’au-delà des fleuves de Koush, au sud de l’Égypte. \q Mon peuple qui avait été dispersé \q {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}apportera des cadeaux.

decisions.choice: the rivers of Cush: the upper Nile, the farthest south
decisions.reason: Cush lay south of Egypt along the Nile and its branches (2:12; Isaiah 18:1). The farthest land known to the south will send worshipers. |

decisions.choice: my worshipers, the daughter of my scattered ones: either scattered Israelites or the peoples of verse 9
decisions.reason: The first word is from the verb "pray, plead", so it means those who pray to the LORD. "The daughter of my scattered ones" may be the LORD's people scattered in exile, brought home by the nations (Isaiah 11:11-12; 66:20), or the peoples of verse 9 themselves, coming with gifts (Isaiah 18:7). The text leaves it open, and the wording keeps both readings possible.

decisions.choice: my offering: a gift brought to the LORD
decisions.reason: The word is used for the grain offering and for tribute brought to a king (Malachi 1:11; Psalm 72:10). |

decisions.choice: those who pray to me, my scattered people (B), My people who were scattered (R); offerings (B), gifts (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "those who pray to me" for "my worshipers" (m2). Balanced and Readable say "people" for the poetic "daughter", as "Daughter Zion" stands for the people of Zion. Readable adds where Cush was, as at 2:12. |

source.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא לֹ֤א תֵב֨וֹשִׁי֙ מִכֹּ֣ל עֲלִילֹתַ֔יִךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּשַׁ֖עַתְּ בִּ֑י כִּי־אָ֣ז׀אָסִ֣יר מִקִּרְבֵּ֗ךְ עַלִּיזֵי֙ גַּאֲוָתֵ֔ךְ וְלֹֽא־תוֹסִ֧פִי לְגָבְהָ֛ה ע֖וֹד בְּהַ֥ר קָדְשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: In that day you will not be ashamed because of all your deeds by which you have transgressed against me; for then I will remove from your midst your proudly exulting [ones], and you will not again be haughty on my holy mountain.

en.L: In that day you will not be put to shame for all your deeds \q by which you transgressed against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q for then I will remove from your midst your proudly exulting ones, \q and you will no longer be haughty on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain.
en.B: On that day you will not be put to shame for all the deeds \q by which you rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q for then I will take away from among you those who proudly exult, \q and never again will you be haughty on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain.
en.R: At that time you will not be ashamed of all the wrong things \q you did when you sinned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q I will take away from among you the people who are proud and boast. \q You will never again be proud on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain.

fr.L: En ce jour-là tu ne seras pas couverte de honte pour toutes tes actions \q par lesquelles tu as transgressé contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ; \q car alors j’ôterai du milieu de toi ceux qui exultent avec orgueil, \q et tu ne seras plus hautaine sur {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} montagne sainte.
fr.B: Ce jour-là, tu n’auras plus à rougir de toutes les actions \q par lesquelles tu t’es révoltée contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, \q car alors j’enlèverai du milieu de toi ceux qui se vantent avec orgueil, \q et jamais plus tu ne seras hautaine sur {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} montagne sainte.
fr.R: En ce temps-là, tu n’auras plus honte de tout le mal \q que tu as fait quand tu as péché contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. \q J’enlèverai du milieu de toi les gens orgueilleux qui se vantent. \q Tu ne seras plus jamais orgueilleuse sur {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} montagne sainte.

decisions.choice: you will not be put to shame: the city is now addressed with promise
decisions.reason: "You" is Jerusalem, Daughter Zion, as in verses 14-20. She will no longer be disgraced by her past, because the LORD has dealt with it (verse 15). |

decisions.choice: your proudly exulting ones: those who boast in their pride
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in Isaiah 13:3 for the LORD's warriors who exult. Here it means the arrogant in Jerusalem, the leaders of verses 3-4, who will be removed. |

decisions.choice: my holy mountain: Zion, where the temple stood
decisions.reason: The temple mount in Jerusalem (Isaiah 2:2-3; Joel 2:1). Pride had no place there. |

decisions.choice: transgressed (L), rebelled (B), sinned (R)
decisions.reason: The verb follows the wording settled for the Twelve. "In that day" follows the Isaiah table. |

decisions.choice: *pashaʿ* "transgresser" (L), "se révolter" (B), "pécher" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for *peshaʿ* and its verb in the Twelve.

source.text: וְהִשְׁאַרְתִּ֣י בְקִרְבֵּ֔ךְ עַ֥ם עָנִ֖י וָדָ֑ל וְחָס֖וּ בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will leave in your midst a people humble and lowly, and they will take refuge in [the] name of Yahweh.

en.L: And I will leave in your midst \q a people humble and lowly, \q and they will take refuge in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I will leave within you \q a people humble and lowly, \q who will take refuge in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: But I will leave among you \q people who are humble and poor. \q They will trust in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to keep them safe.

fr.L: Et je laisserai au milieu de toi \q un peuple humble et pauvre, \q et ils se réfugieront dans le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Je laisserai au milieu de toi \q un peuple humble et pauvre, \q qui cherchera refuge dans le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Mais je laisserai au milieu de toi \q des gens humbles et pauvres. \q Ils compteront sur {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} pour les protéger.

decisions.choice: humble and lowly: poor and powerless, and so dependent on God
decisions.reason: The first word means afflicted or poor, the second weak or lowly. Both describe the powerless, and here also those who are humble before God, the people called to seek humility in 2:3. They take the place of the proud of verse 11. |

decisions.choice: take refuge in the name of the LORD: trust in the LORD himself for protection
decisions.reason: The name stands for the LORD himself as he has made himself known. "The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run into it and are safe" (Proverbs 18:10; compare Psalm 5:12). |

decisions.choice: trust in the LORD to keep them safe (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what taking refuge means (m2). |

source.text: שְׁאֵרִ֨ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל לֹֽא־יַעֲשׂ֤וּ עַוְלָה֙ וְלֹא־יְדַבְּר֣וּ כָזָ֔ב וְלֹֽא־יִמָּצֵ֥א בְּפִיהֶ֖ם לְשׁ֣וֹן תַּרְמִ֑ית כִּֽי־הֵ֛מָּה יִרְע֥וּ וְרָבְצ֖וּ וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] remnant of Israel will not do injustice and will not speak a lie, and there will not be found in their mouth a tongue of deceit; for they will graze and lie down, and there [will be] none making [them] afraid.

en.L: The remnant of Israel will not do injustice and will not speak lies, \q nor will there be found in their mouth a deceitful tongue; \q for they will graze and lie down, and none will make [them] afraid.
en.B: The remnant of Israel will do no wrong and tell no lies; \q no deceitful tongue will be found in their mouths. \q They will graze and lie down, with no one to make them afraid.
en.R: The people of Israel who are left will not do wrong or tell lies. \q They will never try to deceive anyone. \q They will be like sheep that eat and rest, and no one will frighten them.

fr.L: Le reste d’Israël ne commettra pas d’injustice et ne dira pas de mensonges, \q et on ne trouvera pas dans leur bouche de langue trompeuse ; \q car ils paîtront et se coucheront, et personne ne [les] fera trembler.
fr.B: Le reste d’Israël ne fera rien de mal et ne dira pas de mensonges ; \q on ne trouvera pas de langue trompeuse dans leur bouche. \q Ils paîtront et se reposeront, sans personne pour les effrayer.
fr.R: Les Israélites qui resteront ne feront pas le mal et ne diront pas de mensonges. \q Ils n’essaieront jamais de tromper personne. \q Ils seront comme des moutons qui mangent et se reposent, et personne ne leur fera peur.

decisions.choice: will not do injustice: they will be like the LORD
decisions.reason: Verse 5 says that the LORD "does no injustice"; now his people share his character. Revelation 14:5 says of the redeemed that "no lie was found in their mouth". |

decisions.choice: they will graze and lie down, and none will make them afraid: they will live in peace like a well-kept flock
decisions.reason: The remnant is pictured as sheep at pasture. "No one will make them afraid" is a promise of the covenant (Leviticus 26:6; Micah 4:4; Ezekiel 34:28). |

decisions.choice: the remnant of Israel: the people of verse 12
decisions.reason: Zephaniah uses "Israel" for the whole people of God, of whom Judah is what remains. See the note on the remnant at 2:7. |

decisions.choice: like sheep that eat and rest (R)
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture a comparison so that it is not read as about real grazing. |

source.text: רָנִּי֙ בַּת־צִיּ֔וֹן הָרִ֖יעוּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל שִׂמְחִ֤י וְעָלְזִי֙ בְּכָל־לֵ֔ב בַּ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Shout for joy, daughter of Zion; shout, Israel; be glad and exult with all [the] heart, daughter of Jerusalem.

en.L: Shout for joy, daughter of Zion; \q shout aloud, Israel! \q Be glad and exult with all [your] heart, \q daughter of Jerusalem!
en.B: Sing for joy, Daughter Zion; \q shout aloud, Israel! \q Be glad and rejoice with all your heart, \q Daughter Jerusalem!
en.R: Sing for joy, people of Zion! \q Shout, people of Israel! \q Be glad and celebrate with all your heart, \q people of Jerusalem!

fr.L: Pousse des cris de joie, fille de Sion ; \q crie fort, Israël ! \q Réjouis-toi et exulte de tout [ton] cœur, \q fille de Jérusalem !
fr.B: Chante de joie, fille de Sion ; \q pousse des acclamations, Israël ! \q Sois dans l’allégresse et réjouis-toi de tout ton cœur, \q fille de Jérusalem !
fr.R: Chante de joie, peuple de Sion ! \q Crie fort, peuple d’Israël ! \q Sois heureux et fais la fête de tout ton cœur, \q peuple de Jérusalem !

decisions.choice: daughter of Zion, daughter of Jerusalem: the city and its people, pictured as a young woman
decisions.reason: "Daughter Zion" is a name for Jerusalem and its people together (Isaiah 1:8; 62:11). The city condemned in verse 1 is now the one told to rejoice. |

decisions.choice: four calls to rejoice: the judgment is over
decisions.reason: The verse heaps up words for joy: shout, raise a shout, be glad, exult. The reason follows in verse 15. Zechariah 9:9 begins with a call like this. |

decisions.choice: daughter of Zion (L), Daughter Zion (B), people of Zion (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase follows the Isaiah table; "daughter of Jerusalem" follows it the same way. |

decisions.choice: "fille de Sion", "fille de Jérusalem" (L, B); "peuple de Sion", "peuple de Jérusalem" (R)
decisions.reason: The French prophets' settled wording for daughter Zion; Readable names the people, as the English Readable, and Zion is addressed as "tu" through verse 19.

source.text: הֵסִ֤יר יְהוָה֙ מִשְׁפָּטַ֔יִךְ פִּנָּ֖ה אֹֽיְבֵ֑ךְ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל׀יְהוָה֙ בְּקִרְבֵּ֔ךְ לֹא־תִֽירְאִ֥י רָ֖ע עֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh has removed your judgments; he has turned away your enemy. [The] king of Israel, Yahweh, [is] in your midst; you will not fear evil again.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has taken away your judgments; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has cleared away your enemy. \q The King of Israel, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, is in your midst; \q you will not fear evil again.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has taken away the judgments against you; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has turned back your enemy. \q The King of Israel, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, is with you; \q you will never again fear disaster.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has stopped punishing you. \q He has sent your enemies away. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the King of Israel, is with you. \q You will never again be afraid of harm.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a ôté tes jugements ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a écarté ton ennemi. \q Le Roi d’Israël, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, est au milieu de toi ; \q tu ne craindras plus le malheur.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a levé les sentences portées contre toi ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a repoussé ton ennemi. \q Le Roi d’Israël, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, est avec toi ; \q tu ne craindras plus jamais le malheur.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a cessé de te punir. \q Il a chassé tes ennemis. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Roi d’Israël, est avec toi. \q Tu n’auras plus jamais peur du malheur.

decisions.choice: your judgments: the sentences passed against you
decisions.reason: The judgments are the punishments the LORD decreed on the city (verses 6-8). He himself has taken them away. |

decisions.choice: the King of Israel, the LORD, in your midst
decisions.reason: The LORD reigns as Israel's King (Isaiah 33:22; 44:6). He was "in her midst" as judge (verse 5); now he is in her midst to save (verse 17). |

decisions.choice: evil: harm, disaster
decisions.reason: The word covers both wrongdoing and misfortune. Here it is the harm that enemies do. |

decisions.choice: the King of Israel, with a capital K
decisions.reason: "King" is capitalized as a title of God, as in Jeremiah 46:18. Readable says "stopped punishing you" for "taken away your judgments" (m1). |

source.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יֵאָמֵ֥ר לִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֖ם אַל־תִּירָ֑אִי צִיּ֖וֹן אַל־יִרְפּ֥וּ יָדָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: In that day it will be said to Jerusalem, Do not fear, Zion; let not your hands drop.

en.L: In that day \q it will be said to Jerusalem, "Do not fear; \q Zion, let not your hands drop."
en.B: On that day \q they will say to Jerusalem, "Do not be afraid; \q Zion, do not let your hands hang limp."
en.R: At that time \q people will say to Jerusalem, "Do not be afraid! \q Zion, do not lose heart."

fr.L: En ce jour-là \q on dira à Jérusalem : « Ne crains pas ; \q Sion, que tes mains ne faiblissent pas. »
fr.B: Ce jour-là, \q on dira à Jérusalem : « N’aie pas peur ; \q Sion, ne laisse pas tes mains retomber. »
fr.R: En ce temps-là, \q on dira à Jérusalem : « N’aie pas peur ! \q Sion, ne perds pas courage. »

decisions.choice: let not your hands drop: do not lose courage
decisions.reason: Hands that drop are a sign of fear and helplessness (Isaiah 13:7; Jeremiah 6:24); strengthening weak hands means giving courage (Isaiah 35:3). |

decisions.choice: Do not fear, Zion: words taken up in John 12:15
decisions.reason: When Jesus enters Jerusalem on a donkey, John 12:15 quotes Zechariah 9:9 but begins "Do not be afraid, daughter of Zion", words close to this verse and Isaiah 40:9. |

decisions.choice: let not your hands drop (L), hang limp (B), lose heart (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture, Balanced makes it natural English, and Readable says what it means (m1). The words spoken to Jerusalem are in double quotes. |

decisions.choice: "Ne crains pas" (L), as John 12:15
decisions.reason: John 12:15 takes up these words; Literal keeps the published John's "Ne crains pas", while Balanced and Readable use the everyday "N'aie pas peur".

source.text: יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהַ֛יִךְ בְּקִרְבֵּ֖ךגִּבּ֣וֹר יוֹשִׁ֑יעַ יָשִׂ֨ישׂ עָלַ֜יִךְ בְּשִׂמְחָ֗ה יַחֲרִישׁ֙ בְּאַ֣הֲבָת֔וֹ יָגִ֥יל עָלַ֖יִךְ בְּרִנָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh your God [is] in your midst, a warrior who saves; he will rejoice over you with gladness; he will be silent in his love; he will exult over you with a shout of joy.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is in your midst, a warrior who saves; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rejoice over you with gladness, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be silent in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will exult over you with a shout of joy.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is in your midst, a mighty warrior who saves; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will delight in you with gladness and be quiet in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rejoice over you with singing.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is with you, a mighty warrior who will save you; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be very happy with you and rest quietly in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love for you; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will sing and shout for joy over you.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu est au milieu de toi, un guerrier qui sauve ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se réjouira à ton sujet avec allégresse, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se taira dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} exultera à ton sujet avec des cris de joie.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu est au milieu de toi, un vaillant guerrier qui sauve ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fera de toi {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} joie et {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} allégresse, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se reposera en silence dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se réjouira à ton sujet par des chants.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu est avec toi, un vaillant guerrier qui te sauvera ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sera très heureux à cause de toi et se reposera en paix dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour pour toi ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} chantera et criera de joie à cause de toi.

decisions.choice: a warrior who saves: a mighty one who gives victory
decisions.reason: The warrior who cried out bitterly on the day of the LORD (1:14) could not save himself. Here the LORD himself is the warrior, and he saves his people (Isaiah 42:13; Psalm 24:8). |

decisions.choice: he will be silent in his love: his love is quiet and at rest
alternatives: he will renew you in his love
he will quiet you with his love
decisions.reason: The verb means "be silent". It may mean that the LORD's love is too deep for words, or that he rests content in it, or that he will no longer speak of the city's sins. Others read it "he will quiet you by his love". The Greek translation is generally said to read "he will renew you", which in Hebrew differs by one letter. The silence stands between two lines of loud joy.

decisions.choice: the LORD rejoices over his people with shouts of joy
decisions.reason: In verse 14 the people are told to shout for joy; here the LORD himself sings over them. Isaiah 62:5 and 65:19 also speak of God rejoicing over Jerusalem as a groom over his bride. |

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans for every "he" and "his"
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for the LORD in this verse takes the deity_pronoun setting, as set for Zephaniah 3:17. Each clause is joined to the one before, so that no pronoun stands first in a sentence. Balanced says "rejoice over you with singing" for the shout of joy. |

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on every "il" and possessive for the LORD
decisions.reason: As the English, which marks every pronoun in this verse; French spans each "il", "son" and "sa".

source.text: נוּגֵ֧י מִמּוֹעֵ֛ד אָסַ֖פְתִּי מִמֵּ֣ךְ הָי֑וּ מַשְׂאֵ֥ת עָלֶ֖יהָ חֶרְפָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [Those] grieving from [the] appointed feast I have gathered; from you they were, a burden on her, a reproach.

en.L: Those who grieve over the appointed feast I will gather; \q they were from you, a burden on her, a reproach.
en.B: I will gather those who grieve because they are kept from the appointed feasts; \q they are your own, and the disgrace has been a burden on them.
en.R: I will gather those who are sad because they cannot come to the festivals. \q They are your own people, and they have carried the burden of shame.

fr.L: Ceux qui s’affligent loin de la fête fixée, je les rassemblerai ; \q ils étaient de toi, un fardeau sur elle, un opprobre.
fr.B: Je rassemblerai ceux qui s’affligent d’être privés des fêtes fixées ; \q ils sont des tiens, et l’opprobre a pesé sur eux comme un fardeau.
fr.R: Je rassemblerai ceux qui sont tristes parce qu’ils ne peuvent pas venir aux fêtes. \q Ce sont des gens de ton peuple, et ils ont porté le poids de la honte.

decisions.choice: those who grieve over the appointed feast: those who mourn because they cannot keep the festivals
alternatives: as on the day of a festival
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of this verse is very hard, and the ancient translations read it in different ways. The Greek is generally said to join the first words to verse 17 ("as on a day of festival"). The reading taken here keeps the Hebrew words: the LORD will gather those who grieve because they are cut off from the feasts at Jerusalem, and who have borne its disgrace. "I have gathered" is read as a sure promise of what he will do.

decisions.choice: the appointed feasts: Israel's yearly festivals at the temple
decisions.reason: The appointed feasts were the festivals of Leviticus 23, kept at the sanctuary. When the temple was ruined or the people exiled, they could not be kept, and that was a grief in itself (Lamentations 1:4; 2:6). |

decisions.choice: because they are kept from (B), because they cannot come to (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say why they grieve, the sense taken in m1.

source.text: הִנְנִ֥י עֹשֶׂ֛ה אֶת־כָּל־מְעַנַּ֖יִךְ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑יא וְהוֹשַׁעְתִּ֣י אֶת־הַצֹּלֵעָ֗ה וְהַנִּדָּחָה֙ אֲקַבֵּ֔ץ וְשַׂמְתִּים֙ לִתְהִלָּ֣ה וּלְשֵׁ֔ם בְּכָל־הָאָ֖רֶץ בָּשְׁתָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, I [am] dealing with all who afflict you at that time; and I will save the lame and gather the outcast, and I will make them into praise and a name in all the earth [where] their shame [was].

en.L: Look, I am dealing with all who afflict you at that time; \q and I will save the lame and gather the outcast, \q and I will make them a praise and a name \q in all the earth [where] their shame [was].
en.B: At that time I will deal with all who oppress you. \q I will rescue the lame and gather the scattered; \q I will give them praise and honor \q in every land where they were disgraced.
en.R: At that time I will punish everyone who has been cruel to you. \q I will save {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people who are lame and bring home those who were driven away. \q In every land where people laughed at them, \q I will make them praised and honored.

fr.L: Voici, je vais agir contre tous ceux qui t’oppriment, en ce temps-là ; \q et je sauverai la boiteuse et rassemblerai la rejetée, \q et je ferai d’eux une louange et un nom \q dans toute la terre [où était] leur honte.
fr.B: En ce temps-là, j’agirai contre tous ceux qui t’oppriment. \q Je sauverai les boiteux et rassemblerai les dispersés ; \q je leur donnerai louange et renom \q dans tous les pays où ils ont été couverts de honte.
fr.R: En ce temps-là, je punirai tous ceux qui ont été cruels envers toi. \q Je sauverai les membres boiteux de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple et je ramènerai chez eux ceux qui avaient été chassés. \q Dans tous les pays où l’on se moquait d’eux, \q je ferai qu’on les loue et qu’on les honore.

decisions.choice: the lame and the outcast: the scattered flock gathered home
decisions.reason: The words are feminine and singular, picturing the people as a flock with its weak and strayed sheep. Micah 4:6-7 makes the same promise in nearly the same words, and Ezekiel 34:16 has the shepherd seek the lost and bind up the injured. |

decisions.choice: a praise and a name: renown and honor
decisions.reason: To have a name is to be honored and famous. Deuteronomy 26:19 and Jeremiah 13:11 use the same words for what Israel was meant to be for the LORD; Jeremiah 33:9 promises it again. |

decisions.choice: in all the earth where their shame was: in the lands where they were disgraced
decisions.reason: The last words, "their shame", are joined to "all the earth": the places where they were put to shame will now see them honored. |

decisions.choice: deal with (L, B), punish (R); the scattered (B), driven away (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "punish" for "deal with", which in this setting means to deal with in judgment. Readable makes the sheep picture plain by calling them the LORD's people. |

decisions.choice: "la boiteuse", "la rejetée" (L), feminine as the Hebrew; "les boiteux", "les dispersés" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew participles are feminine singular, the flock pictured as one ewe (as Micah 4:6-7); Literal keeps the form, and the other levels say who is meant.

source.text: בָּעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ אָבִ֣יא אֶתְכֶ֔ם וּבָעֵ֖ת קַבְּצִ֣י אֶתְכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־אֶתֵּ֨ן אֶתְכֶ֜ם לְשֵׁ֣ם וְלִתְהִלָּ֗ה בְּכֹל֙ עַמֵּ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ בְּשׁוּבִ֧י אֶת־שְׁבוּתֵיכֶ֛ם לְעֵינֵיכֶ֖ם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: At that time I will bring you [in], and at [the] time of my gathering you; for I will make you a name and a praise among all [the] peoples of the earth, when I restore your fortunes before your eyes, says Yahweh.

en.L: At that time I will bring you [home], \q even at the time when I gather you; \q for I will give you as a name and as a praise among all the peoples of the earth, \q as I restore your fortunes before your eyes, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: At that time I will bring you home, \q at the time when I gather you. \q I will make you honored and praised among all the peoples of the earth \q as I restore your fortunes before your very eyes, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: At that time I will gather you and bring you home. \q I will make all the nations of the earth honor you and praise you. \q You will see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} make things good for you again, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

fr.L: En ce temps-là je vous ferai [revenir], \q au temps où je vous rassemblerai ; \q car je ferai de vous un nom et une louange parmi tous les peuples de la terre, \q quand je rétablirai votre sort sous vos yeux, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: En ce temps-là, je vous ramènerai chez vous, \q au temps où je vous rassemblerai. \q Je ferai de vous un peuple honoré et loué parmi tous les peuples de la terre, \q quand je rétablirai votre sort sous vos yeux mêmes, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: En ce temps-là, je vous rassemblerai et je vous ramènerai chez vous. \q Je ferai que toutes les nations de la terre vous honorent et vous louent. \q Vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} verrez vous rendre de nouveau heureux, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

decisions.choice: at that time I will bring you home: the promise of verse 19 said again, now to the people
decisions.reason: "You" is now plural: the LORD speaks to the people themselves. The repetition of "at that time" makes the promise sure. |

decisions.choice: before your eyes: you will see it yourselves
decisions.reason: Those who are scattered will live to see their own restoration. |

decisions.choice: restore your fortunes: give back what was lost
decisions.reason: As in 2:7, the phrase may mean restoring prosperity or bringing back exiles; here, after "I will gather you", both are meant. |

decisions.choice: restore your fortunes (L, B), make things good for you again (R); says the LORD
decisions.reason: The phrase follows the Jeremiah table. "Says the LORD" closes the book at every level. |

decisions.choice: "vous" (plural) in verse 20, after "tu" for Zion
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" is plural in this verse, the scattered people, so French changes to "vous".
